struct: A user-defined type whose members are **public by default**; otherwise identical to a `class`. Objects may be declared between the closing brace and the semicolon: `struct product { int weight; double price; } apple, banana;`. See [Structs, classes and the four OOP words](#/comp3522-w3/structs-classes).
class: A user-defined type that bundles data members and member functions; members are **private by default**. Defined with `class Name { ... };` and its member functions are defined outside with the scope operator, `double Circle::area()`. See [Structs, classes and the four OOP words](#/comp3522-w3/structs-classes).
encapsulation: Combining data members and functions into one unit (the class), making the data private and providing public getters and setters. See [Structs, classes and the four OOP words](#/comp3522-w3/structs-classes).
abstraction: Showing the user only the relevant details and hiding the rest: access specifiers inside a class, and header files across files (you call `pow()` without knowing how it is implemented). See [Structs, classes and the four OOP words](#/comp3522-w3/structs-classes).
public|public:: Access specifier: the member is accessible anywhere. Also the usual inheritance kind, `class Bus : public Vehicle`, which keeps inherited members at their own level. See [Inheritance, access levels, which constructor runs](#/comp3522-w3/inheritance).
protected|protected:: Access specifier: accessible inside the class and inside classes derived from it, not from outside. Protected inheritance caps every inherited member at protected. See [Inheritance, access levels, which constructor runs](#/comp3522-w3/inheritance).
private|private:: Access specifier: accessible only from within the class itself; never accessible from a derived class. Private inheritance (`class X : private Spy`, and the default for `class X : Spy`) caps every inherited member at private. See [Inheritance, access levels, which constructor runs](#/comp3522-w3/inheritance).
Circle::|::: The **scope operator**. `double Circle::area()` defines, in the source file, the member function declared inside `class Circle` in the header; `var.Base::print()` calls the base class's version of a virtual function explicitly. See [Structs, classes and the four OOP words](#/comp3522-w3/structs-classes).
constructor: A member function with the class's name and **no return type** that runs when an object is created. Declaring any constructor removes the compiler-generated default one. See [Constructors, member initialization, default arguments](#/comp3522-w3/constructors).
default constructor: A constructor that takes no arguments or has default values for every argument, so `Circle c;` compiles. The slides recommend defining one whenever the type has a natural default state. See [Constructors, member initialization, default arguments](#/comp3522-w3/constructors).
most vexing parse: `Circle my_circle();` does not create an object: it declares a function named `my_circle` returning a Circle. Write `Circle my_circle;` or `Circle my_circle{};`. See [Constructors, member initialization, default arguments](#/comp3522-w3/constructors).
member initialization list|initializatio: The `: radius(r), i(0)` part between a constructor's parameter list and its body. Members are initialized here, before the body runs, **in declaration order** regardless of the list's order. Class-type members left out are default-constructed. See [Constructors, member initialization, default arguments](#/comp3522-w3/constructors).
default arguments|default argument: Values supplied in a prototype for **trailing** parameters only (`Complex(double r = 0, double i = 0)`), written in the header, not repeated in the source. `char *= nullptr` is an error: the space between `*` and `=` matters. See [Constructors, member initialization, default arguments](#/comp3522-w3/constructors).
const member function|const: A member function declared with `const` after its parameter list (`double area() const`) promises not to modify the object's members; the compiler rejects attempts to. Use it on every getter. See [Constructors, member initialization, default arguments](#/comp3522-w3/constructors).
copy constructor: The constructor that builds a new object from an existing one: `Complex(const Complex& c) : r(c.r), i(c.i) {}`. Called by `Complex d(c);` and `Complex d = c;`, not by `d = c;` (that is the assignment operator). The compiler generates a member-wise (shallow) one. See [The copy constructor: shallow versus deep](#/comp3522-w3/copy-constructor).
shallow copy: What the compiler-generated copy constructor does with a pointer member: it copies the address, so two objects share one array. A write through one changes the other, and two destructors free the array twice. See [The copy constructor: shallow versus deep](#/comp3522-w3/copy-constructor).
deep copy: A copy constructor that allocates new storage (`data(new double[size])`) and copies the elements, so each object owns its own array. See [The copy constructor: shallow versus deep](#/comp3522-w3/copy-constructor).
destructor|~: The member function `~Complex()` (no parameters, no return type) that runs automatically when an object's lifetime ends: end of scope, `delete`, or program termination. It frees what the object acquired, typically `delete[] data`. See [Destructors and object lifetime](#/comp3522-w3/destructor).
forward declaration: `class Car;`: tells the compiler a class by that name exists without defining it. Enough to declare `Car*` or `Car&`, not a `Car` by value (incomplete type). Breaks circular includes. See [Forward declarations and organizing code](#/comp3522-w3/forward-declaration).
incomplete type: The error `field 'owner' has incomplete type` when a forward-declared class is used by value before its definition; the compiler cannot know its size. Use a pointer or reference. See [Forward declarations and organizing code](#/comp3522-w3/forward-declaration).
base class: The class being inherited from (Java: superclass). Its constructor runs first when a derived object is built. See [Inheritance, access levels, which constructor runs](#/comp3522-w3/inheritance).
derived class: The class that inherits (Java: subclass): `class Bus : public Vehicle`. It inherits all accessible members except constructors, the destructor, friends and private members. See [Inheritance, access levels, which constructor runs](#/comp3522-w3/inheritance).
polymorphism: From the Greek for many forms: one call to a member function runs different functions depending on the type of the object, through a base pointer or reference and a virtual function. See [Polymorphism and virtual functions](#/comp3522-w3/polymorphism-virtual).
virtual: Keyword on a base class member function that allows a derived class to redefine it and makes calls through base pointers and references use the derived version: dynamic binding, late binding, polymorphic dispatch. See [Polymorphism and virtual functions](#/comp3522-w3/polymorphism-virtual).
override: Optional keyword on a derived class's function that asks the compiler to check that it really overrides a virtual function of the base with the same signature. See [Polymorphism and virtual functions](#/comp3522-w3/polymorphism-virtual).
dynamic binding|late binding: Choosing which function to run at run time from the object's actual type, which `virtual` enables for calls through pointers and references. See [Polymorphism and virtual functions](#/comp3522-w3/polymorphism-virtual).
polymorphic class: A class that declares or inherits a virtual function. See [Polymorphism and virtual functions](#/comp3522-w3/polymorphism-virtual).
slicing|object slicing: Copying a derived object into a base object (`Polygon poly2 = rect;`) keeps only the base part, so calls on the copy run the base version even if the function is virtual. Polymorphism only works with pointers or references. See [Polymorphism and virtual functions](#/comp3522-w3/polymorphism-virtual).
assert|assert(): Macro from `<cassert>` that evaluates an expression and terminates the program if it is false; used to check preconditions, postconditions and invariants. `#define NDEBUG` before the include turns it off. See [Testing and debugging](#/comp3522-w3/testing-debugging).
equivalence partition|equivalence partit: Groups of inputs the code processes the same way, made disjoint so each test exercises exactly one; for 100–999 the deck tests 50, 100, 500, 999, 1500. See [Testing and debugging](#/comp3522-w3/testing-debugging).
regression testing: Re-running the whole test suite whenever a bug is fixed (after adding a test for it), because fixing new bugs can reintroduce old ones. See [Testing and debugging](#/comp3522-w3/testing-debugging).
TEST_CASE: Catch macro that defines one independent test: `TEST_CASE("description", "tag") { ... }`. Each runs as if it were its own main. See [Lab 3: MyStack and Catch unit tests](#/comp3522-w3/lab3-stack).
REQUIRE: Catch macro that asserts an expression is true inside a test case and reports the line and expression when it is not. See [Lab 3: MyStack and Catch unit tests](#/comp3522-w3/lab3-stack).
CATCH_CONFIG_MAIN: Defined before `#include "catch.hpp"` in exactly one source file, it makes Catch generate the `main` that runs every test case; your own main must be commented out. See [Lab 3: MyStack and Catch unit tests](#/comp3522-w3/lab3-stack).
composition: UML: a class is made up of objects of another and the parts cannot exist without the whole (filled diamond at the whole): an order and its order_items. See [UML review](#/comp3522-w3/uml-review).
aggregation: UML: a class references objects of another that live on when it is destroyed (hollow diamond at the whole): a pond and its ducks. See [UML review](#/comp3522-w3/uml-review).
generalization: UML inheritance: a solid line with a hollow triangle at the base class, A is a subclass of B. See [UML review](#/comp3522-w3/uml-review).
realization: UML: a dashed line with a hollow triangle; A implements the interface B. See [UML review](#/comp3522-w3/uml-review).
dependency: UML: a dashed arrow; A has methods that use B without necessarily holding an instance. See [UML review](#/comp3522-w3/uml-review).
lifeline: In a sequence diagram, one participant: its name and class in a box on top and a dotted vertical line marking its place in time; activations are the thin rectangles on it. See [UML review](#/comp3522-w3/uml-review).
